title: Kurdish-Led SDF Announces Formal Dissolution After Completing Merger With Syrian Army
detail: August 25, 2026 — SDF commander Mazloum Abdi announced the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces has formally dissolved as an independent military force after completing its merger with the Syrian army, declaring "the end of the SDF's mission" now that Syria has "entered a new phase, one of peace and participation in building a new Syria." The dissolution follows through on the Jan 29, 2026 Damascus-SDF agreement and the integration process SDF said was complete on Aug 20; the merger deal also formalizes recognition of Kurdish cultural, civil and educational rights — including Kurdish as a national language, Nowruz as an official holiday, and citizenship for previously stateless Kurds. The SDF, once the US's principal partner against ISIS, lost most of its northeast Syria territory to a government offensive in January before agreeing to merge with Damascus's forces under interim President Ahmad al-Sharaa.

title: Board of Peace Warns Both Israel and Hamas Over Gaza Ceasefire Compliance Amid Kite Dispute
detail: August 25, 2026 — In a rare public rebuke, an official from the US-backed Board of Peace overseeing the October 2025 Gaza ceasefire told Reuters that "all militant activity in Gaza must stop, including the flying of kites," but also warned Israel that "military action cannot extend beyond responding to genuine and imminent threats," after Israel complained to the Board about roughly a dozen incendiary kites and four balloons that crossed into Israeli border communities during August (the military said nothing dangerous was found attached). Gaza's local popular committees, which run displacement camps, urged parents to stop children flying kites to avoid giving Israel a pretext for renewed strikes. IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir said Israel's pursuit of Oct 7 suspects "continues" and it "will take every opportunity to eliminate threats," while US officials voiced concern that Israel's elastic definition of "imminent threat" risked undermining the Board's disarmament-and-withdrawal roadmap. A Hamas official said the group has told mediators Israel is using "fake pretexts" to keep striking Gaza.

title: Pakistan Reports 'Significant Progress' Mediating Iran-US Talks to Revive Islamabad MOU
detail: August 24-25, 2026 — Pakistan's army chief Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi made a daylong diplomatic mission to Tehran, meeting President Masoud Pezeshkian, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei to discuss reviving the June 17 Islamabad MOU, whose 60-day negotiating window had lapsed Aug 17 without a deal. Naqvi said the talks "concluded on a highly positive note," with both sides reviewing steps to restore the MOU framework, and that Pakistan remains "hopeful this momentum will help pave the way for further progress and lasting peace in the region." Discussions focused on measures to prevent further escalation, reopening the Strait of Hormuz to normal tanker traffic, and an expedited end to the conflict. Pezeshkian said "the United States must correct its tone and approach," warning that American "intimidation" could complicate any MOU revival — the visit came days after Trump's Aug 20 'economic D-Day' sanctions threat and Bessent's Aug 24 sanctions rollout.
